svg.title: Turn admission and locking, session side
svg.desc: A request for one session runs through TurnManager.reserveTurn inside a per-session arrival-order chain: ExecutionCoordinator.acquire runs TurnRunner.admitTurn (budget check, session lock and global cap, loop check, rate-limit wait), then takes a lane permit. Only then does reserveAdmittedTurn write the turn id to turn_state.json; settlement deletes it and releases the lock. TaskExecutor enters at acquire, outside the chain.

g.text: Hover a box for what it does; its connections light up. Click it to open its section.
A red chip is the exception that refuses the turn at that step. The harness half is in control-protocol.md.

svg.text: Turn admission and locking, session side
A turn is admitted in a fixed order, and its crash marker is written only after every gate has passed.

g.text: web chat, channel, cron, logical agent; task and workflow enter at 2
callers · every surface reaches TurnManager.startTurn or reserveTurn
TaskExecutor skips the per-session chain and calls ExecutionCoordinator.acquire plus reserveAdmittedTurn directly.
tasks and workflow steps: outside the chain
TaskExecutor · calls ExecutionCoordinator.acquire and reserveAdmittedTurn directly
A task request is fail-fast: it takes its lane permit before admission, so one that finds no permit runs none of the checks.
same-session reservations run through the chain,
then the session is read: provider, policy, surface
A later request for the same session cannot overtake an earlier one during the session read, governance checks, lock or permit.
lane: primary or provider worker; runs admission
ExecutionCoordinator.acquire · execution_coordinator.dart passes TurnRunner.admitTurn as the shared admitExecution hook
Fail-fast task and workflow requests take their lane permit before admission; every other request is admitted first, then takes its permit.
read-only daily budget, before the lock
checkBudget · TurnGovernanceEnforcer.checkBudget throws under action block
It reads usage only and records nothing, so it may run before the lock.
SessionLockManager.acquire · waits while the session is locked, then throws BusyTurnException(isSameSession: false) at the cap
A cap rejection has recorded nothing yet, because the checks that record state run after it.
chain depth, token velocity; records the start
checkLoopPreTurn · records state, so it runs only after the cap admitted the attempt
LoopAction.abort throws LoopDetectedException; a throw here releases the lock taken in b.
defers while the global turn rate is reached
awaitRateLimitWindow · polls once a second while holding the cap slot
A throw from c or d releases the session lock; a wait here keeps its lane position.
WorkerCapacityGate permit; fail-fast requests take it before admission
lane permit and lease · worker_capacity_gate.dart via ExecutionCoordinator._acquirePrimary and _acquireWorker
No permit means BusyTurnException for provider capacity, and the admission is released.
one lock per session, activeCount <= maxParallel
SessionLockManager · concurrency/session_lock_manager.dart; one instance is shared by every runner
Reconfigurable on server.*; a raise wakes callers parked in whenCapacityAvailable(), which reserves nothing.
The set call is synchronous (secureWriteFileSync) although the call site is unawaited, so a rejected request leaves no marker.
executeTurn · TurnRunner.executeTurn launches the harness turn
The harness half of the lifecycle is Control Protocol section 6.
queue releases its next item if completed
settlement · turn_runner_execution_loop.dart finally block and ConversationService._observeOutcome
A failed or cancelled turn holds the remaining conversation queue instead of releasing it.
{ sessionId: { turnId, startedAt } }, one record per active turn
turn_state.json · TurnStateStore in dartclaw_core storage; mutations are synchronous atomic writes and open quarantines malformed JSON
A record that survives a crash is removed by detectAndCleanOrphanedTurns at the next serving start, which flags the session.
